title: Biomolecular Detection employing the Interferometric Reflectance Imaging Sensor (IRIS)
protocol: Prepare polymer solution by adding 100 mg of copoly(DMA-NAS-MAPS) to 5 mL of deionized water.
Add 5 mL of 40% saturated ammonium sulfate solution to reach a final concentration of 0.92 M in the polymer solution.
Submerge silicon-SiO2 substrates in the polymer solution for 30 min on a shaker.
Rinse substrates thoroughly with deionized water.
Dry substrates thoroughly with Argon/N2 gas.
Bake substrates at 80 °C for 15 min.
Store polymer-coated substrates in a dry environment (vacuum desiccator) for up to 3 months until probe spotting procedure.
Dilute probes, such as antibodies or antigens, to an appropriate concentration in desired buffer.
Typically use antigen or IgG at a concentration of 0.5 mg/mL in phosphate buffered saline (PBS) with pH ≈7.4.
Place diluted probe solutions in a 96- or 384-well plate for subsequent spotting procedure.
Setup spotting parameters for desired printed array.
Determine appropriate spotting parameters for surface and solutions (dwell times, approach speeds).
Determine number of replicates per grid, grid layout, replicate grids, and spotting location on chip.
Place substrates and source plate in appropriate locations.
Check waste and supply bottles are ready.
Begin printing run.
After spotting is finished, place substrates in high humidity environment overnight (4-18 hours).
Wash substrates in PBST for three minutes.
Wash substrates in PBS for three minutes.
Wash substrates in DI water for three minutes.
Dry chip thoroughly with Argon gas if wet experiment.
Deactivate remaining NHS groups on copolymer surface by submerging chips in 50 mM ethanolamine pH 7.4 for 30 minutes while shaking.
Alternatively, use a primary amine-containing compound such as hydroxylamine or Tris.
Rinse deactivation solution with PBS then DI water thoroughly.
Make a solution of BSA in PBS as the target of interest.
Prepare an equivalent amount of buffer without the target for negative control incubation.
Take a silicon mirror scan to normalize subsequently collected data.
Scan the prepared probe array with the IRIS system prior to incubation to determine initial optical height at each spot.
Submerge chip(s) in the prepared solution on a shaker plate for 1 hour.
Repeat the wash procedure described in step 2.5.
Scan the probe array using the IRIS system after incubation.
Obtain post-incubation images for pre-incubation comparison.
Fit collected images from each IRIS scan with lab-developed software to produce an optical thickness image of the probe array.
Subtract registered post- and pre-incubation images for a qualitative analysis of binding.
Determine mass densities of each spot compared to the background by averaging optical thickness information within spots and annuli outside spots.
Reconstitute human serum albumin (HSA)-specific antibodies.
Create difference images for the binding array to assess binding qualitatively.
Conduct quantitative analysis to measure optical height changes.
Incubate with HSA spots and rabbit IgG control spots.
Measure mean optical height change of 2.05 nm for HSA spots.
Measure mean optical height change of 0.13 nm for rabbit IgG spots.
Perform IRIS measurement of Fur protein binding dependence on protein concentration.
Measure absolute optical heights for initial immobilized oligomer probe heights and post-incubation Fur binding.
Incubate with increasing concentrations of Fur (50, 100, 200 nM).
Increase the length of dsDNA oligomers to observe impact on Fur binding.
Calculate Fur protein dimer binding per dsDNA strand.
